observation: d_min=0.03 worsened MAPE from 0.3114 to 0.4846. Lowering d_min allowed gentler terminal decline but the fitter produced a worse hindcast, suggesting this well needs a higher terminal decline rate, not lower. The flat late-life production may be better captured by forcing earlier exponential transition.

d_min=0.08 worsened MAPE further to 0.5385 with R2=-2.58. Both lower (0.03) and higher (0.08) d_min values hurt significantly. d_min=0.05 appears near-optimal for this well. Moving to other parameters.

d_min=0.04 also worsened MAPE to 0.411. All three d_min experiments (0.03, 0.04, 0.08) degraded from baseline 0.05. d_min is settled at 0.05. Moving to qi_guess_strategy next — the well has multiple workovers creating new peaks, so first-month qi=643 may not represent the dominant decline regime.

qi_guess_strategy=max3 produced identical results to baseline — optimizer converges to same solution (qi=1507, di=0.87, b=2.0) regardless of initial qi guess. The fit is dominated by the optimizer bounds, not initial guesses.

di_initial=0.90 produced identical results — optimizer converges to same solution regardless of starting point. Fitting initial conditions do not matter for this well. Moving to preprocessing parameters.

outlier_threshold=0.15 improved MAPE from 0.3114 to 0.3069. Outlier rejection rate dropped from 8.2% to 6.9% (fewer but more targeted rejections with tighter threshold). Fit months increased from 346 to 351, suggesting cleaner data kept more usable months. First improvement found — preprocessing quality matters more than fitting params for this noisy well.

smoothing_window=5 produced identical results to v7. The smoothing window does not affect the fit for this well — the decline curve fitting likely applies its own smoothing or the outlier rejection already handles the noise.

outlier_window=5 worsened MAPE to 0.3137. Wider window increased rejection rate to 9.3% (from 6.9%), removing too many legitimate data points and reducing fit months from 351 to 342. The 3-month window is better for this well.

significance_threshold=0.40 improved MAPE significantly from 0.3069 to 0.282. R2 in-sample dropped from 0.61 to 0.40 (fitting fewer noisy points) but hindcast accuracy improved — filtering out low-significance production segments removes noise that was distorting the decline curve. Fit months dropped from 351 to 344.

significance_threshold=0.35 was far too aggressive — fit months dropped from 344 to 225, losing too much production history. MAPE spiked to 0.6517. The sweet spot is at 0.40; going lower removes legitimate decline data. R2 in-sample improved to 0.71 but hindcast was terrible because the model overfit a truncated dataset.
peak_merge_distance=5 produced identical results. Peak merging does not affect this well's fit — the dominant decline phases are already well-separated.
